title: OTP fraud - bank vs customer liability disputes
p1:
Your phone rings. Someone says they are from your bank. Minutes later, money disappears from your account.

But who is responsible — the bank or the customer?
p2:
Many people believe that sharing an OTP automatically means the customer has to bear the loss. That is not always the full story.

OTP is a security layer, but banks also have responsibilities to maintain safe systems and respond to fraud risks. The details of each case matter, including how the fraud happened and whether the customer acted carelessly.
p3:
A surprising point: reporting an unauthorized transaction quickly can affect your rights. Delays in informing the bank may create complications, while timely reporting can strengthen your position.

The practical lesson is simple — never share OTPs, and if fraud occurs, immediately contact your bank and document every step.
conclusion: Have you ever faced an OTP fraud attempt, and do you think banks or customers should carry more responsibility in such cases?
